question.prompt: If the equation \(\frac{m}{x-2}+3=\frac{1-x}{2-x}\) in \(x\) has an extraneous solution, what is the value of \(m\)?

solutions.explanation: Clearing the denominators gives \(m+3(x-2)=x-1\). The extraneous solution can only be \(x=2\). Substituting gives \(m+0=1\), so \(m=1\).
solutions.title: Use the excluded value in the cleared equation
